questions.question: Which of the following is a function of money?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All options are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The function of Money is :

 
 
• Medium of exchange
 
• Unit of account
 
• Store of value
 
 
 
• Medium of Exchange: When money is used to intermediate the exchange of goods and services, it performs a function of a medium of exchange.
 
• Unit of Account: It is a standard unit of measurement of the market value of goods, services, and other transactions.
 
 
• It is a standard of relative worth and deferred payment and is a necessary prerequisite for the formulation of commercial agreements that involve debt.
 
 
 
• Store of Value: When the money is reliably saved, stored, and retrieved it acts as a store of value.

questions.question: Who was the contemporary ruler of Emperor Asoka in Sri Lanka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tissa.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tissa (Devanampiya Tissa)** was the contemporary ruler of Ashoka in Sri Lanka.
 
• After adopting Buddhism, **Ashoka spread Buddhism in nine other countries** along with Sri Lanka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Ashoka:

 
• He was the **son of **the Mauryan emperor **Bindusara** and the **grandson of Chandragupta Maurya.**
 
• His **other names were Devanampiya **(Sanskrit Devanampriya meaning Beloved of the Gods) and **Piyadasi.**
 
• He is considered one of **India’s greatest emperors.**
 
• He was born in 304 BC.
 
• His reign lasted from 268 BC to 232 BC when he died.
 
• At its zenith, Ashoka’s empire stretched **from Afghanistan in the west to Bangladesh** in the east.
 
• It covered almost the whole Indian subcontinent except present Kerala and Tamil Nadu, and modern-day Sri Lanka.
 
• His capital was at Pataliputra (Patna) and had provincial capitals at Taxila and Ujjain.

questions.question: Isobars are atoms of different chemical elements that have ________.

options.text: Same atomic number but different mass number
Same mass number but different atomic number
Same mass number and same atomic number

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Same mass number but different atomic number.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Isobars: The nuclei which have the same mass number (A) but a different atomic number (Z) are called isobars.
 
• Examples of Isobars are 14 C 6, 14 N 7
 
 
• From above it is clear that the nuclei which have the same mass number (A) but a different atomic number (Z) are called isobars.
 
• Isobars occupy different positions in the periodic table so all isobars have different chemical properties, but the same physical properties.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Isotopes: The atoms of an element having the same atomic number but a different mass number are called isotopes.

 
 
• All isotopes have the same chemical properties.
 
 
 
• Isotones: The nuclei having an equal number of neutrons are called isotones. For them both the atomic number (Z) and mass number (A) are different, but the value of (A – Z) is the same.

questions.question:
Gram Panchayat is composed of which of the following?

I. The ward panchs

II. The sarpanch

III. The district collector

Codes:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I and II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Gram panchayat** is the grassroots level of panchayat raj formalized local self-governance system in India.​
 
• Gram Panchayat consists of **a village or a group of villages** divided into smaller units called **“Wards”.**
 
• Each ward selects or elects a representative who is known as the **Panch** or **ward member**.
 
• The members of the Gram Sabha elect the** ward members** through a **direct election.**
 
• The **Sarpanch** or the president of the Gram Panchayat is elected by the ward members as per the State Act. 
 
• **The Sarpanch and the Panch** are elected for a period of **five years.**
 
• Gram Panchayat is governed by the elected body and administration.
 
• **The secretary** is normally in charge of the administrative duties of the Gram Panchayat.

Thus, we can conclude that **Gram Panchayat is composed of Ward Panch and Sarpanch.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct decreasing order of intercellular space in various simple permanent tissues?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parenchyma > Collenchyma > Sclerenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Simple Permanent Tissue** is also known as homogenous tissues.
 
• They are made up of a single cell type, usually with the same origin, structure, and function.
 
• **Simple permanent tissue is further classified into three types**: 
 
 
• **Parenchyma **-
 
 
• It is composed of living cells that are thin-walled, unspecialized in structure, and therefore adaptable, with differentiation, to various functions.
 
• The cells are found in many places throughout plant bodies and, given that they are alive, are actively involved in photosynthesis, secretion, food storage, and other activities of plant life.
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma **-
 
 
• It supports the tissue of living elongated cells with irregular cell walls.
 
• It has thick deposits of cellulose in its cell walls and appears polygonal in cross-sections.
 
• The strength of the tissue results from these thickened cell walls and the longitudinal interlocking of the cells.
 
• It may form cylinders or occur as discrete strands and is one of the three ground, or fundamental, tissues in plants, together with parenchyma (living thin-walled tissue) and sclerenchyma (dead support tissue with thick cell walls).
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma**
 
 
• It supports tissue composed of any of various kinds of hard woody cells.
 
• Mature sclerenchyma cells are usually dead cells that have heavily thickened secondary walls containing lignin.
 
• The cells are rigid and nonstretchable and are usually found in nongrowing regions of plant bodies, such as the bark or mature stems.
 
• It is one of the three types of ground, or fundamental, tissue in plants; the other two types are parenchyma (living thin-walled tissue) and collenchyma (living support tissue with irregular walls).
 
• Its occur in many different shapes and sizes, but two main types occur fibers and sclereids.

questions.question: When the vibrating object moves forward, it creates a region of high pressure in the medium called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**compression.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• When a vibrating object moves forward, it pushes and compresses the air in front of it creating a region of high pressure. This region is called Compression and this starts to move away from the vibrating object.
 
• When a vibrating object moves backwards, it creates a region of low pressure. This region is called Rarefaction. 
 
• As the object moves back and forth creates a series of compression and rarefaction in the air and this makes the sound wave propagates through the medium.

questions.question: The _________ keeps the average temperature of the Earth fairly steady.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The atmosphere helps in keeping the temperature of the earth at steady levels.
 
• During day time atmosphere prevents the temperature from getting too high and during night time it does not allow heat to escape the earth, in this way a fairly steady temperature is maintained throughout the year on earth.
 
• The air is a poor conductor of heat. During the day, it prevents a sudden increase in the temperature of the earth and prevents the heat from escaping to outer space during the night. It keeps the average temperature of the earth steady. Moon has no atmosphere and the temperature ranges from 121°C during the day to -157°C at night.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Biosphere-**

 
• Biosphere refers to the narrow zone between the **lithosphere, atmosphere, and hydrosphere** where life exists.
 
• The biosphere consists of living organisms both plants and animals. Here, the physical environment (lithosphere, atmosphere, and hydrosphere) interacts with each other and supports life. It is also known as the ecosphere.

**Heliosphere-**

 
• The heliosphere is the region surrounding the Sun and the solar system is filled with the solar magnetic field and the protons and electrons of the solar wind.
 
• The heliosphere shields the solar system from galactic cosmic radiation. 

**Photosphere-**

 
• The photosphere is the lowest layer of the sun's atmosphere. the innermost layer we can observe directly.
 
• The term photosphere means "sphere of light" and is the layer where most of the sun's energy is emitted.
 
• It takes about eight minutes for sunlight from the photosphere to reach Earth.
